mainEntity.name: Will I feel pain during dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implant surgery is performed under local anaesthesia, which numbs the treatment area effectively. Most patients do not experience pain during the procedure itself. You may feel pressure, vibration, or a sense of movement — these are normal sensations that are separate from pain. If at any point you experience genuine discomfort, signalling your dental team allows them to respond immediately. Individual experiences vary, and your dental team will discuss what to expect during your pre-operative appointment.

mainEntity.name: Why does dental implant surgery make so much noise?

acceptedAnswer.text: The sounds associated with implant surgery are produced by the precision instruments used to prepare the bone site and place the implant. These include mechanical drills, irrigation equipment, and the ratcheting tools used to secure the implant. Bone also conducts vibration through the skull, which can make sounds feel more prominent than expected. These sounds are entirely normal and are not indicators of discomfort or complication. If you are particularly sensitive to procedural sounds, discuss this with your dental team beforehand.

mainEntity.name: How long does dental implant surgery take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The duration of a single implant placement appointment varies depending on the complexity of the case, how many implants are being placed, and whether any preparatory procedures — such as bone grafting — are required. A straightforward single implant placement may take between one and two hours. Your dental team will give you a clear indication of the expected appointment length during your consultation, as this depends entirely on your individual clinical situation.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to feel anxious before implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely. Dental anxiety before implant surgery is very common, particularly concerns about procedural sounds, sensations, and the unknown aspects of the experience. Acknowledging this anxiety openly with your dental team is always encouraged. Dental professionals are trained to support anxious patients and can adapt their communication, pacing, and approach accordingly. Many patients report that the procedure was considerably more straightforward than they had anticipated once they understood what to expect.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if I experience problems after implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild swelling, tenderness, and bruising in the days following implant placement are expected and normal. If symptoms are worsening rather than improving after the first few days, or if you notice signs such as increasing pain, fever, discharge from the surgical site, or the implant feeling loose, contact your dental team promptly. Early assessment is always preferable to waiting. Your dental team will advise you on the appropriate next steps based on your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: How soon can I return to normal activity after dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many patients return to light activities and desk-based work the following day, although this varies individually. Strenuous physical activity is generally advisable to avoid for several days following surgery, as this can affect healing and increase the risk of bleeding. Your dental team will provide specific guidance tailored to your case, including when you can return to your normal diet, exercise routine, and oral hygiene practices. Always follow the personalised aftercare instructions provided at your appointment.
